481: B is correct because the write-through caching strategy writes data to the cache and the database at the same time whenever a customer adds or updates an item, which keeps the cache data always in sync with the database. Lazy loading only populates the cache on reads and can serve stale data, while TTL-based approaches still permit temporary mismatches between cache and database.
482: B is correct because AWS DataSync automates the migration of the 100 GB of historical data over the existing 100 Mbps connection, and it encrypts all data in transit with TLS by default, meeting the encryption requirement. It also handles scheduling, retries, and data integrity verification with minimal manual effort, making it lower overhead than CLI sync jobs or a VPN, and 100 GB is far too small to justify a Snowball device.
483: C is correct because Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate supports Windows containers and scheduled tasks, so the job runs serverlessly every 10 minutes and the company pays only for the 1 to 3 minutes of runtime. AWS Lambda cannot run the job because Lambda container images only support Linux, not Windows, and AWS Batch with Fargate does not support Windows workloads. Using Windows task scheduler to launch standalone tasks would add external orchestration overhead instead of using ECS's native scheduling.
484: A is correct because creating an organization in AWS Organizations with all features turned on lets the company consolidate existing accounts and centrally create the new AWS accounts for each business unit. E is correct because AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) can be set up in that organization and integrated with the company's corporate directory service to provide centralized authentication across all the accounts. Together these two actions deliver consolidated multi-account management plus centralized directory-based single sign-on.
485: A is correct because S3 Glacier with Expedited retrievals typically makes archived objects available in 1 to 5 minutes, meeting the five-minute restore requirement, while Glacier storage costs far less than the IA tiers for rarely accessed archives. Standard retrievals from Glacier take 3 to 5 hours and would miss the requirement, and S3 Standard-IA or One Zone-IA storage costs significantly more for rarely restored data.
486: A is correct because Amazon S3 provides simple, highly available, low-cost static website hosting with no servers to manage for the presentation tier. Amazon ECS with AWS Fargate runs the containerized logic tier without provisioning or patching any servers, and a managed Amazon RDS cluster removes database administration overhead. EKS with Fargate adds Kubernetes complexity without benefit for this workload, and options based on EC2 or CloudFront as the static host increase operational cost and management effort.
487: C is correct because Amazon EFS is a highly available and automatically scalable NFS file system that multiple Linux instances can mount simultaneously in AWS and on premises through the Site-to-Site VPN, and it grows and shrinks on demand with no minimum size. Deploying multiple mount targets, one per Availability Zone, provides high availability across AZ failures. EBS Multi-Attach is single-AZ block storage that is not a mountable file system, a single mount target is a single point of failure, and FSx is not the native Linux NFS solution for this scenario.
488: C is correct because a service control policy that denies access to billing information, attached to the root organizational unit, applies to every account in the organization and can restrict even the root user of member accounts, which no IAM policy can do. Identity-based policies cannot restrict root users, and an organization that is using the all features feature set cannot be converted back to the consolidated billing feature set.
489: C is correct because an Amazon SNS dead-letter queue captures the order messages that fail delivery to the on-premises HTTPS endpoint, and an Amazon SQS queue used as the DLQ target supports a message retention period of up to 14 days so the undelivered messages can be retained and analyzed. This uses only existing service configuration with no application changes, whereas a Kinesis Data Stream target adds cost and development effort, a DynamoDB table is not a supported DLQ target, and inserting an SQS queue between the application and SNS requires re-architecting the flow.
490: B is correct because the Amazon DynamoDB export to Amazon S3 feature uses point-in-time recovery data to export the table to S3 without consuming any read capacity units and without affecting the availability of the table, and enabling point-in-time recovery provides the continuous backups of the data. This requires minimal setup and no coding, unlike Lambda functions with DynamoDB Streams or scheduled exports that need custom development, and an EMR cluster with Hive is heavy and consumes table capacity when reading data.
491: A is correct because an Amazon SQS standard queue guarantees at-least-once delivery, which matches the requirement to process each request at least once, and standard queues are cheaper than FIFO queues. Server-side encryption with an AWS KMS key (SSE-KMS) protects the credit card data at rest, and the kms:Decrypt permission on the Lambda execution role is the required permission that lets the event source mapping read and decrypt the encrypted messages. The FIFO options cost more without adding needed value, and encryption key invocation permission is not the permission the execution role requires.
492: B is correct because AWS Organizations allows the company to group the development accounts into organizational units and attach a service control policy that restricts which EC2 instance types can be created, and SCPs are enforced centrally across all accounts in those OUs with no development effort. The alternatives based on Systems Manager templates, EventBridge with Lambda remediation, or AWS Service Catalog products all require building and maintaining custom automation and processes.
493: D is correct because Amazon Transcribe is the managed service that converts the customer service call recordings in any language into text. E is correct because Amazon Translate then converts that text from any language into English, allowing the company to support current and future languages without maintaining its own models. F is correct because Amazon Comprehend analyzes the English text and produces the written sentiment analysis reports, and all three are fully managed AI services so no machine learning model maintenance is required.
494: D is correct because the IAM policy allows the terminate action only under the condition that the request originates from the CIDR blocks 192.0.2.0/24 or 203.0.113.0/24, so a request from any other source IP address is denied with a 403 error. The policy does grant the required EC2 termination actions, and identity-based policies do not need to specify a principal, so the only reason for the denial is the unmet source IP condition.
495: C is correct because Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security service that runs discovery jobs using managed data identifiers to automatically detect sensitive data such as PII, passport numbers, and credit card numbers in S3 buckets. It works with the S3 data backing the Lake Formation data lake and produces findings without writing custom queries. Audit Manager assesses compliance controls rather than data content, and S3 Inventory with Athena or S3 Select would require significant manual query development to identify sensitive data.
496: B is correct because an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway exposes an NFS interface backed by Amazon S3 and provides local caching, so the NFS workloads keep functioning unchanged while gaining scalable AWS-backed storage with high performance. D is correct because a Storage Gateway volume gateway provides iSCSI block storage backed by EBS with local caching, replacing the block storage in the same no re-architecting way. The remaining options are either temporary migration appliances or do not provide native protocols with local caching for both block and NFS storage.
497: C is correct because a VPC gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 routes the traffic from the private subnet to S3 over the AWS private network, bypassing the NAT gateway entirely and eliminating its per-GB data processing charges for the large volume of S3 traffic. Gateway endpoints are free, highly available, and require only a route table configuration, unlike managing dedicated NAT instances or paying for an additional NAT gateway.
498: A is correct because S3 Lifecycle rules can automatically expire noncurrent object versions and retain only the two most recent versions, running natively on the bucket as a set-and-forget configuration with no code or manual operations. A Lambda function or S3 Batch Operations approach requires building, scheduling, and maintaining custom jobs, and versioning cannot be deactivated on a bucket once it has been enabled.
499: D is correct because a 200 Mbps hosted connection ordered through an AWS Direct Connect Partner matches the company's low utilization of under 10% and costs far less than the 1 Gbps port while providing the same private and secure connectivity. Sub-1 Gbps connection speeds are only available as hosted connections through Direct Connect Partners, so the company cannot provision a 200 Mbps dedicated connection itself in the console, and dedicated connections cannot simply be shared with another AWS account.
500: A is correct because AWS DataSync transfers data directly from the on-premises Windows file servers to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server while preserving file data, shares, and NTFS permissions and ACLs, so access rights remain unchanged, and scheduled tasks automate the migration. D is correct because an AWS Snowcone device can host the AWS DataSync agents on premises, which is useful where deploying virtual machine resources is difficult, and the DataSync tasks still move the data with permissions preserved into FSx for Windows File Server. The options that stage the data in Amazon S3 do not preserve NTFS file permissions and add unnecessary extra steps.
